en: For my health, I try not to eat sweet things.
why: Only ために can follow の, and を must sit between the noun and the verb before ようにする.

en: From next year, I decided to live in Japan.
why: The place takes に, the verb comes next, and こと comes right before にしました.

after: いて、{全然|ぜんぜん}{勉強|べんきょう}しません。
en: My little brother does nothing but play games every day and doesn't study at all.
why: The pattern is ～てばかりいる, so して comes right before ばかり, and ゲームを is the object of して.

en: I have just now finished eating lunch.
why: The pattern is た-form + ところです, with the object and を first.

after: ですが、あまり{食|た}べません。
en: It's not that I dislike meat, but I don't eat it much.
why: The set pattern is な-adjective + なわけではない.

after: を{思|おも}い{出|だ}します。
en: Every time I hear this song, I remember my childhood.
why: The verb must follow を, then たびに, and {子|こ}どもの must come before ころ.

en: You should go to many countries while you are young.
why: {若|わか}いうちに is a set pattern, いろいろな goes before the noun, and た-form comes before ほうがいい.

en: Table manners differ from country to country.
why: によって is one pattern, and {食事|しょくじ}の must come before マナー.

before: {明日|あした}の{会議|かいぎ}では、
en: At tomorrow's meeting, we will discuss the new product.
why: The adjective goes before the noun, and について follows the noun.

en: I am saving money in order to study abroad.
why: ために follows the verb, then object, then the て-form and います.

before: {後|うし}ろの{席|せき}の{人|ひと}にも
en: Please speak so that people in the back seats can hear too.
why: ように follows the plain verb, and ～てください ends the sentence.

before: {荷物|にもつ}は{昨日|きのう}{送|おく}ったので、
en: I sent the package yesterday, so it should arrive by tomorrow.
why: には follows the time word, and the plain verb comes before はずです.

en: According to the weather forecast, it will snow tomorrow.
why: によると is a set phrase, and ～になる comes right before らしい.

before: {部屋|へや}の{電気|でんき}が{消|き}えているから、
en: The room's light is off, so it seems he is already asleep.
why: もう comes first, {寝|ね}ている is one verb form, and みたい follows it.

en: Because I stayed up late last night, I have a headache.
why: {遅|おそ}くまで modifies the verb {起|お}きていた, and せいで follows it.

before: {先生|せんせい}が{教|おし}えてくれた
en: Thanks to my teacher's help, I was able to pass a difficult exam.
why: おかげで follows the verb, the adjective goes before {試験|しけん}, and に goes before {合格|ごうかく}.

en: From next month, I will work at the Osaka branch.
why: {大阪|おおさか}の must come before {支店|してん}, and the verb comes before ことになる.

en: Today I made dinner instead of my mother.
why: の is followed by かわりに, the subject takes が, and {夕食|ゆうしょく} takes を.

en: Even when I do it exactly as the manual says, it doesn't work well.
why: {書|か}いてある is one form, とおりに follows it, and やっても comes last.

en: I like cooking while listening to music.
why: ながら follows the ます-stem, and する must come before のが.

en: The more you read this book, the more interesting it gets.
why: The pattern is ～ば～ほど, and the adjective comes before なります.

en: This morning I left home without eating breakfast.
why: ずに follows the stem {食|た}べ, and を links the noun and the verb.

before: {明日|あした}は{大切|たいせつ}な{試験|しけん}なので、
en: Tomorrow is an important exam, so I can't take the day off.
why: The set pattern is verb + わけにはいかない.

before: {終電|しゅうでん}が{行|い}ってしまったので、
en: The last train has gone, so I have no choice but to go home by taxi.
why: で follows タクシー, and しか comes after the verb, before ありません.

en: This summer is much hotter than last summer.
why: {去年|きょねん}の goes before {夏|なつ}, then に{比|くら}べて.

en: For me, the most important thing is my family.
why: にとって follows わたし, and いちばん must come before {大切|たいせつ}.

en: Mr. Yamada is kind to everyone.
why: The pattern is だれに{対|たい}しても.

en: My older brother works as an elementary school teacher.
why: {小学校|しょうがっこう}の goes before {先生|せんせい}, and として follows the noun.

after: {電話|でんわ}で{聞|き}いてみます。
en: I'll call and ask whether this store is open on Sundays too.
why: も follows {日曜日|にちようび}, and かどうか follows the verb.

en: Today is not as cold as yesterday.
why: The pattern is noun + ほど + negative adjective.

en: The moment I left home, it started to rain.
why: とたんに follows the た-form, and {雨|あめ}が is the subject of {降|ふ}り{出|だ}した.

en: While I was out shopping, I also borrowed a book from the library.
why: ついでに follows the verb, and {本|ほん} must come right before を.

en: I started learning the guitar last spring.
why: はじめる attaches to the ます-stem {習|なら}い.

en: I finished reading the book I borrowed from my friend and returned it right away.
why: {借|か}りた modifies {本|ほん}, and きる attaches to the stem {読|よ}み.

en: What time does tomorrow's meeting start again?
why: {明日|あした}の needs a noun after it, and だった comes right before っけ.

before: ニュースによると、{来月|らいげつ}から
en: According to the news, train fares will go up from next month.
why: {電車|でんしゃ}の goes before {料金|りょうきん}, and the verb comes before ということです.

en: Please take this medicine every six hours.
why: おきに follows the time length, and ～てください ends it.

en: I feel like I have met this person before.
why: The set pattern is ～ような{気|き}がする.

before: まだ{時間|じかん}があるから、
en: There's still time, so there's no need to hurry so much.
why: The set pattern is verb + ことはない.

en: I think promises should be kept.
why: べき follows the plain verb, then だと{思|おも}います.

before: {明日|あした}から{夏休|なつやす}みなので、
en: Summer vacation starts tomorrow, so I can't wait.
why: The set pattern is ～てしかたがない.

before: この{店|みせ}の{料理|りょうり}は
after: は、とてもおいしいです。
en: The food at this restaurant is very good for such a low price.
why: The pattern is ～わりには, after the adjective {安|やす}い.

before: {弟|おとうと}は{自分|じぶん}では
after: {文句|もんく}ばかり{言|い}います。
en: My brother complains all the time even though he does nothing himself.
why: {何|なに}もしない is a set phrase, and くせに follows the verb.

before: {寝坊|ねぼう}して、もう{少|すこ}しで
en: I overslept and almost missed my plane.
why: {乗|の}り{遅|おそ}れる is one verb, and に marks the plane.

before: {毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}して、
en: By practicing every day, I became able to read kanji.
why: The pattern is potential verb + ようになる.

en: Excuse me, could you carry this bag for me?
why: この must come before {荷物|にもつ}, and ～てもらえませんか is the request form.

en: Expensive things are not always good things.
why: {高|たか}い needs a noun after it, and とは{限|かぎ}りません ends the sentence.

before: {兄|あに}は{母|はは}に{呼|よ}ばれても、
en: Even when my mother called him, my older brother pretended to be asleep.
why: {寝|ね}ている is one form, then ふりをする.

after: 、{世界中|せかいじゅう}を{旅行|りょこう}したいです。
en: If I only had the money and time, I would travel all over the world.
why: と links two nouns, and さえ comes before あれば.

en: My mobile phone rang right in the middle of the meeting.
why: の needs {最中|さいちゅう} after it, and {携帯|けいたい} goes before {電話|でんわ}.

before: {電気|でんき}がついているから、{林|はやし}さんは
en: The light is on, so Ms. Hayashi must be at home.
why: {家|いえ}に goes before いる, and に{違|ちが}いない follows the verb.

en: If it was going to be this crowded, I should have come earlier.
why: The pattern is ～ばよかった, with {来|く}れ before ば.

en: When I'm busy, I sometimes don't eat lunch.
why: The negative verb comes before ことがある.

en: My mother told me she wants me to clean my room.
why: {自分|じぶん}の goes before {部屋|へや}, and ほしい follows the て-form.

before: {体|からだ}の{調子|ちょうし}が{悪|わる}かったので、
en: I wasn't feeling well, so I was allowed to take the day off work.
why: The pattern is causative て-form + もらう.

after: 、{友|とも}だちから{電話|でんわ}が{来|き}ました。
en: Just as I was about to leave home, a call came from a friend.
why: The pattern is volitional + とする, then ときに.

en: If you get tired, it's fine to go home first.
why: {先|さき}に is one phrase, and ～てもかまわない is a set pattern.

en: She can speak not only English but also Chinese.
why: The pattern is A ばかりでなく B も.

en: I was so busy I didn't even have time to drink water.
why: {水|みず}を{飲|の}む modifies {時間|じかん}, and さえ follows the noun.

en: Please hand in this report by next Friday.
why: {来週|らいしゅう}の goes before {金曜日|きんようび}, and までに follows the date.

before: {一生懸命|いっしょうけんめい}{勉強|べんきょう}した
en: Even though I studied very hard, I failed the exam.
why: のに follows the verb, and ～てしまいました ends the sentence.

en: The doctor told me not to drink alcohol.
why: The pattern is ～ないようにと{言|い}われる.

en: I make it a rule not to look at my phone before bed.
why: The negative verb comes before ことにしている.

before: {外|そと}が{暗|くら}くなってきました。
en: It's getting dark outside. It seems it has started to rain.
why: {降|ふ}り{出|だ}した is one verb, and ようです follows it.

before: {田中|たなか}さんの{話|はなし}では、
en: According to Mr. Tanaka, Ms. Yamada is getting married.
why: が marks the subject, and the plain verb comes before そうです.

en: I want to become a person like Mr. Tanaka too.
why: みたいな needs a noun after it, and に comes before なりたい.

en: People say these clothes look a bit childish.
why: っぽい attaches to {子|こ}ども, and と comes before {言|い}われます.

en: Because of the typhoon, tomorrow's game was canceled.
why: ために follows の, {明日|あした}の goes before {試合|しあい}, and {中止|ちゅうし} comes before になる.

en: Which bus should I take to get to the station?
why: どの must come before バス, and ～ばいい is the pattern.

before: この{寮|りょう}では、{夜|よる}
en: In this dormitory, you have to be back by 10 p.m.
why: までに follows the time, and the verb comes before ことになっている.

en: Children tend to want to copy adults.
why: {大人|おとな}の goes before まね, and たがる attaches to the stem し.

before: お{客|きゃく}さんが{来|く}る{前|まえ}に、
en: I will clean the room before the guests come.
why: The pattern is ～ておく, with the object and を first.

en: I fell asleep with the window open.
why: The pattern is た-form + ままで, then the next verb.

before: {十年|じゅうねん}も{日本|にほん}に{住|す}んでいたなら、
en: If he lived in Japan for ten years, no wonder his Japanese is good.
why: The な-adjective takes な before わけです.

before: {雨|あめ}の{中|なか}で{遊|あそ}んだので、
en: They played in the rain, so the children's clothes got covered in mud.
why: {子|こ}どもたちの goes before {服|ふく}, and だらけ attaches to どろ.

en: I like Japanese food such as sushi and tempura.
why: や links すし to the next noun, and ような comes before the noun it describes.

en: This castle is said to have been built by a king long ago.
why: {昔|むかし}の goes before {王様|おうさま}, and によって comes before the passive verb.

en: I'd like to climb Mt. Fuji once.
why: The pattern is ～てみたい, with に marking the mountain.

en: No matter how much I think, I can't figure out the answer.
why: The pattern is いくら～ても, and the subject {答|こた}えが comes before わかりません.

en: If you had told me, I would have helped you.
why: The pattern is ～てくれれば～てあげたのに.
